description.value: A tidy highway wayside on the Buckinghorse River at km 278 of the Alaska Highway, offering river swimming, arctic grayling fishing, and reliable moose and bear sightings in the northern Rocky Mountain foothills; cooperatively managed with basic facilities and a gate-controlled season from late May through September.

address.value: Mile 175 Rd, Peace River, BC V0C 2V0, Canada

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The BC Parks website confirms this is an active frontcountry campground on the Alaska Highway (km 278, ~200km NW of Fort St. John), cooperatively managed with a community partner. OSM tags (tents=yes, fee=yes) are corroborated by the website's camping context. The website explicitly notes e-bikes are prohibited on trails and restricted to roads only; no amenity details (water, showers, food storage, etc.) are described on the park page.
concerns: No phone number or civic address in OSM or on the park-specific webpage; general BC Parks contact (1-800-689-9025) exists but is not campground-specific.
Cooperatively managed by a community/society partner — services and facilities may be non-standard and are not enumerated on the website.
Grizzly and black bears are described as frequently present in the surrounding area; no bear-safe food storage facilities are confirmed.
E-bikes are explicitly prohibited on trails and restricted to park roads only — relevant for e-bike tourers.
Very remote location (~200 km NW of Fort St. John); no food or services nearby are mentioned.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, active BC Parks campground on the Alaska Highway that is a logical and valuable overnight stop for northbound touring cyclists; remote location increases its value as one of few services in the area.
enrichment_extras.notes: The website confirms tents are permitted (corroborating OSM tents=yes). No amenity details such as water, showers, laundry, or electrical hookups are described on the park page, leaving most optional amenities unverifiable.
